description:
🌐 **A provider outage burns the stall budget and marks sound work INCOMPLETE.** Measured on talos, 2026-08-24. `71-real-game-supply-decision` ran three consecutive iterations whose ENTIRE output was `API Error: 529 Overloaded. This is a server-side issue, usually temporary`. Chief counted each as *"no progress"*, hit `stall 3/2`, printed *"Chief stalled 3 iterations after its 5-iter budget without completing. Stopping."* and left the branch INCOMPLETE. `72-godot-ci-containerized-build-lane` died the same way two iterations later.

**The agent never ran.** A 529 is the API refusing the request — no turn was taken, no tool was called, nothing was attempted. Counting it as a failed attempt conflates *"the agent tried and got nowhere"* with *"the agent was never given a chance"*, and only the first is evidence about the work.

**The cost is real and it is silent.** `71` was 1/2 with its remaining story most of the way done — the adopted game (`lampe-games/godot-open-rts @ a628ad3`, decided and recorded in US-001) had already been fetched into `dogfood/open-rts/`, 2,029 files, correctly placed and not gitignored. The run died before any of it could be committed, so `chief ps` reported `✗ failed`, `no progress last iter`, on a tasklist whose work was sitting intact in the worktree. An operator reading that display would reasonably conclude the tasklist was broken and re-scope it.

**This is distinct from the stall the counter exists for.** A genuine stall — the agent runs, produces a turn, and the story count does not move — is exactly the signal chief should act on, and `71`'s own iteration 2 (`progress (1/2 passing)`) shows the mechanism works when the agent actually runs. Nothing here weakens that. What must change is that an iteration which never reached the model is not counted as one that did.

**Retry is the other half.** The message itself says *"usually temporary — try again in a moment"*, and chief has no backoff for it: three iterations fired into an overloaded API back to back, wasting the budget in the time a single wait would have covered. The repo already reasoned this through for a DIFFERENT surface — `cuneiform/365-transient-provider-failure-backoff` split provider failures into transient vs permanent and honoured `Retry-After` — and the same distinction applies to chief's own driver.

userStories.title: An iteration that never reached the model does not count as an attempt
userStories.description: The core defect. A 529 means no turn was taken; counting it as a failed attempt is a category error.
acceptanceCriteria: An iteration whose agent invocation failed BEFORE the model produced a turn — provider unavailable (429/500/502/503/529), a connection failure, or an auth/quota refusal — does not increment the stall counter and does not count against the iteration budget. The tasklist's state is unchanged by it, because nothing happened

The condition is detected from the invocation's OUTCOME, not by grepping prose for `API Error`. A vendor rewording its message must not silently re-break this. If a text match is unavoidable it is a documented list with the observed message recorded beside each entry and the date it was seen — a match-on-prose rule whose observations are not written down cannot be audited when it stops firing, and a silently-stopped classifier reads exactly like the bug this tasklist fixes.

A genuine stall is UNCHANGED: the agent runs, produces a turn, and the story count does not move — that still increments the counter and still stops the run at the threshold. `71`'s iteration 2 (`progress (1/2 passing)`) and iterations 3-5 (529, no turn) must be classified differently, and a test asserts exactly that pair

The run summary distinguishes the two in its OUTPUT: a tasklist stopped by provider unavailability is not reported as `✗ failed … no progress last iter`, which is what sent an operator to re-scope a tasklist whose work was intact
userStories.notes: bash -n clean on bin/chief + engine/*.sh + install.sh + test/*.sh + templates/verify.sh. shellcheck -S error (0.10.0): 0 errors on every file this story touched (engine/quality.sh + engine/sweep.sh report 3 errors that are pre-existing on main). VERSION 0.8.88 -> 0.8.89 + README bold v0.8.89; test/version-bump.sh PASS, test/doc-sync.sh PASS. NEW test/provider-unavailable.sh PASS, 3 parts: (1) 14 classification fixtures — 529 observed message / structured overloaded_error / pretty-printed "status":503 / 502 / 500 / ECONNRESET / socket hang up / 401 all exit 8, while the no-progress turn, a non-provider crash and 529-text-with-rc-0 still exit 1 and a 429 rate_limit_error + usage-limit prose still exit 2, and PROVIDER_NOTURN_LIMIT=0 restores exit 1. (2) THE PAIR in one run: iteration 1 scored 'progress (1/2 passing)', the 529 iterations produced ZERO 'no progress (stall' lines, iteration 2 was announced 3x (budget uncharged), 4 provider calls, exit 8, committed work + banked pass-state intact. (3) Under the real driver: status 'PROVIDER-UNAVAILABLE 0/1', scheduler state 'provider-unavailable', summary says 'PROVIDER UNAVAILABLE ... not failed and not stalled', neither run log nor worker log contains 'no progress' or 'INCOMPLETE', branch kept and nothing retired. Regression sweep green: smoke, ratelimit, limitstate, limitresume, limitmonitor, headless, events, liveliness, noworkguard, stall-flag, doc-sync, version-bump = 12 PASS, 0 FAIL.

userStories.title: A transient provider failure is WAITED OUT, not fired into three times
userStories.description: The message says "try again in a moment" and chief has no backoff. Three iterations were spent inside the window a single wait would have covered.
acceptanceCriteria: A provider-unavailable outcome is retried with exponential backoff and jitter under a stated cap, and `Retry-After` is honoured when the provider sends one, in both its forms (delta-seconds and HTTP-date) — the provider naming its own interval is better information than any backoff computed here
The wait is OBSERVABLE in `chief ps` and in the run log: a tasklist waiting on the provider says so, with the delay and the attempt count, rather than appearing to work or appearing hung
The cap and the retry limit together bound the worst-case wall time to a figure recorded in the story notes, and `0` disables waiting so the pre-fix behaviour stays reachable for debugging

A permanent refusal — bad credentials, a revoked key, a quota that will not replenish — FAILS FAST with its reason rather than sleeping through a budget it cannot satisfy. Where the two cannot be told apart the run treats it as transient and says so, the fail direction chosen from cost: waiting on a permanent error wastes minutes, while failing fast on an outage loses the tasklist

Driven against a stub that returns 529 with `Retry-After`, 529 without it, a connection reset, and a 401 — asserting the measured elapsed wait (not a mocked clock), the stall counter staying at zero across all the transient cases, and the fail-fast on 401
userStories.notes: WORST-CASE WALL TIME: (PROVIDER_NOTURN_LIMIT-1) x PROVIDER_BACKOFF_CAP = with the defaults (3, 60s) at most 2 waits of at most 60s = 120s of waiting before the run reports the block. bash -n clean on bin/chief + engine/*.sh + install.sh + test/*.sh + templates/verify.sh. shellcheck -S error (0.10.0): 0 errors on every file touched. VERSION 0.8.89 -> 0.8.90 + README bold v0.8.90. NEW test/provider-backoff.sh PASS (27s, every wait MEASURED on the real clock via date +%s around the loop and per-call epoch stamps from the stub, no mocked clock): Retry-After: 4 -> 6s measured / 2 calls; an HTTP-date Retry-After -> 5s measured; Retry-After: 86400 clamped to the 3s cap; no header -> waits of 2s then 3s (7s measured, 3 calls) and the delay grows; stall counter 0 in the log AND stall=0 in the live record across all transient cases; chief ps renders "provider-backoff for 0s - US-1 - iter 1 - retry at 19:01 (in 7s) - provider attempt 2/3"; ECONNRESET retried after a 2s wait with "could not be told apart - treating it as transient" in the log; 401 authentication_error = 1 call, 1s, no "Waiting" line, ".provider-unavailable" says "PERMANENT refusal, not retried"; PROVIDER_BACKOFF=0 = 3 calls in 2s with no wait. Regression sweep green: version-bump, doc-sync, stall-flag, provider-backoff, provider-unavailable, smoke, ratelimit, noworkguard, liveliness, limitstate, limitresume, limitmonitor, headless, events, monitor, monitor-orphan, pause, five-cases = 18 PASS, 0 FAIL. scripts/check-doc-links.mjs: 0 dead references.

userStories.title: Work already on disk is never described as no work
userStories.description: `71` reported `✗ failed` while 2,029 correctly-placed files sat uncommitted in its worktree. The display drove the wrong conclusion.
acceptanceCriteria: When a run ends INCOMPLETE, the summary reports whether the worktree holds UNCOMMITTED changes and roughly how much — so `left in worktree for review` names what is actually there instead of leaving an operator to discover 2,029 files by hand
`chief ps` distinguishes `no work produced` from `work produced but not committed`. The first is a real signal and the second is a recoverable state, and today they render identically

The check is cheap and never fails the run: a `git status --porcelain` in the worktree, reported best-effort, with any error swallowed. This is a reporting improvement and must not become a new way for a run to die
A test asserts the specific regression: a worktree with staged and unstaged changes, whose run ended INCOMPLETE, renders as work-pending rather than as no-work

NEW test/worktree-pending.sh PASS (registered in verify.sh + all.sh + ci.yml), 4 parts: (1) worktree_pending() read — clean tree -> '', and a missing path / a non-git dir / /dev/null / no argument ALL -> '' and exit 0 under set -e; an untracked DIRECTORY counted per file ("9 uncommitted file(s) (7 untracked, 1 modified, 1 staged) · added.txt, kept.txt, dogfood/") and the counts survive a rename + a multi-byte path. (2) The regression under the real driver: INCOMPLETE 1/2 with work standing on disk -> wp.pending = "work pending: 7 uncommitted file(s) (5 untracked, 1 modified, 1 staged) · dogfood/, out/ — produced but NOT committed; nothing is lost (git -C <wt> status)", worker log says "holds UNCOMMITTED work", summary prints the "WORK LEFT UNCOMMITTED — 1 tasklist(s)" block + "NOTHING IS LOST", branch kept with US-1's commit. (3) The clean INCOMPLETE says so rather than going silent ("no uncommitted work: everything this run produced is committed on the branch") and does NOT appear in the block. (4) chief ps against a synthetic registry: two `failed` rows, one rendering "work pending: 2029 uncommitted file(s) … · dogfood/" and the other "no work produced: nothing committed, and nothing uncommitted in the worktree either" — asserted to be DIFFERENT lines.
